steps.say: Systemic mastocytosis is clonal neoplastic proliferation of abnormal mast cells in bone marrow and extracutaneous organs. More than ninety to ninety five percent of adult patients harbor the activating somatic point mutation KIT D816V in exon seventeen, which confers intrinsic resistance to imatinib. KIT locked on means imatinib bounces off.
steps.tx: **Systemic mastocytosis** is clonal neoplastic proliferation of abnormal mast cells in bone marrow and extracutaneous organs. More than **90% to 95%** of adult patients harbor the activating somatic point mutation **KIT D816V** in exon 17, which confers intrinsic resistance to imatinib. KIT locked on means imatinib bounces off.

vis.alt: KIT D816V mast cell with mediator release, dense marrow aggregates, urticaria pigmentosa with Darier sign, and multiorgan infiltration.
vis.caption: KIT mutation, dense aggregates, Darier sign and organ infiltration. Percentages are in the text, not on the drawing (StewardMD).

steps.say: The major diagnostic criterion for systemic mastocytosis is multifocal dense infiltrates of fifteen or more mast cells in bone marrow or extracutaneous tissue. Minor criteria include atypical spindle-shaped morphology, aberrant expression of CD25 or CD2 by mast cells, KIT D816V mutation, and baseline serum total tryptase persistently exceeding twenty nanograms per millilitre. Fifteen in a cluster is the major.
steps.tx: The major diagnostic criterion for systemic mastocytosis is multifocal dense infiltrates of **15 or more mast cells** in bone marrow or extracutaneous tissue. Minor criteria include atypical **spindle-shaped** morphology, aberrant expression of **CD25** and/or CD2 by mast cells, **KIT D816V** mutation, and baseline serum total tryptase persistently exceeding **20 ng/mL**. Fifteen in a cluster is the major.

rows: Multifocal dense infiltrates of 15 or more mast cells

steps.say: Hypereosinophilic syndrome is defined by absolute blood eosinophil count exceeding one thousand five hundred per microlitre on two occasions at least one month apart, exclusion of secondary causes such as parasitosis, drug allergy and vasculitis, and objective documentation of eosinophil-mediated organ damage. High counts alone are not the syndrome; damage completes it.
steps.tx: **Hypereosinophilic syndrome** (HES) is defined by absolute blood eosinophil count exceeding **1,500 per microlitre** on two occasions at least **1 month** apart, exclusion of secondary etiologies (parasitosis, drug allergy, vasculitis), and objective documentation of **eosinophil-mediated organ damage** (cardiac endomyocardial fibrosis, thromboembolism, neuropathy, pulmonary infiltrates). High counts alone are not the syndrome; damage completes it.

vis.alt: Eosinophil count criteria, FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion, end-organ damage map, and imatinib, steroid and mepolizumab therapy boxes.
vis.caption: Counts, fusion, damage and therapies in one panel. The drawing phrases timing as months or occasions; the lesson teaches two occasions at least one month apart (StewardMD).

steps.say: The myeloproliferative variant of hypereosinophilic syndrome is driven by a cryptic interstitial deletion on chromosome 4q12 resulting in the constitutively active FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion tyrosine kinase. These patients have splenomegaly, elevated serum tryptase and cardiac involvement, and exhibit exquisite responsiveness to low-dose imatinib at one hundred milligrams daily. Fusion kinase is melted by imatinib.
steps.tx: The **myeloproliferative variant** of hypereosinophilic syndrome is driven by a cryptic interstitial deletion on chromosome **4q12** resulting in the constitutively active **FIP1L1-PDGFRA** fusion tyrosine kinase. These patients have **splenomegaly**, elevated serum tryptase and cardiac involvement, and exhibit exquisite responsiveness to low-dose imatinib (**100 mg daily**). Fusion kinase is melted by imatinib.

steps.say: Mepolizumab, a fully humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody directed against interleukin five, is approved for patients with severe PDGFRA-negative hypereosinophilic syndrome and eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis. Interleukin five is the key cytokine regulating eosinophil survival, differentiation and trafficking. Block the survival signal and eosinophils fade.
steps.tx: **Mepolizumab**, a fully humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody directed against **IL-5**, is approved for patients with severe **PDGFRA-negative** hypereosinophilic syndrome and eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA). IL-5 is the key cytokine regulating eosinophil survival, differentiation, and trafficking. Block the survival signal and eosinophils fade.

steps.say: Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms occurs two to eight weeks after exposure, classically allopurinol, aromatic antiepileptics, sulfasalazine and vancomycin. It shows extensive morbilliform eruption, facial edema, fever, marked eosinophilia, atypical lymphocytosis, internal organ involvement such as hepatitis and nephritis, and human herpesvirus 6 reactivation. Weeks later, face swollen, organs failing.
steps.tx: **Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms** (DRESS syndrome) occurs **2 to 8 weeks** after exposure (classically **allopurinol**, aromatic antiepileptics, **sulfasalazine**, vancomycin). It shows extensive **morbilliform eruption**, **facial edema**, fever, marked eosinophilia, **atypical lymphocytosis**, internal organ involvement (hepatitis, nephritis), and **HHV-6 reactivation**. Weeks later, face swollen, organs failing.

vis.alt: Facial edema with periorbital swelling, morbilliform rash, and blood film with eosinophils and atypical lymphocytes in DRESS.
vis.caption: Facial swelling, rash and blood film in DRESS. Drugs and timing are in the text, not on the drawing (StewardMD).

steps.say: Eosinophilic fasciitis, Shulman disease, is painful symmetrical induration of the skin and subcutaneous tissues of the forearms and legs, sparing the digits, often following strenuous physical exercise. Hallmarks include the groove sign with linear depressions along superficial veins when the limb is elevated, peripheral eosinophilia, and deep en bloc full-thickness biopsy showing marked fascial thickening. Grooves where veins run, fingers spared.
steps.tx: **Eosinophilic fasciitis** (Shulman disease) is painful symmetrical **induration** of the skin and subcutaneous tissues of the forearms and legs, **sparing the digits**, often following strenuous physical exercise. Hallmarks include the **groove sign** (linear depressions along superficial veins when the limb is elevated), peripheral eosinophilia, and deep en bloc full-thickness biopsy showing marked **fascial thickening**. Grooves where veins run, fingers spared.

vis.alt: Forearm with groove sign and peau d'orange skin sparing the hand, plus block showing thickened deep fascia over muscle.
vis.caption: Groove sign with hand sparing and thickened fascia. The biopsy requirement is in the text, not on the drawing (StewardMD).

steps.say: Avapritinib is a selective KIT and PDGFRA activation-loop mutant kinase inhibitor approved for advanced systemic mastocytosis, demonstrating potent clinical responses and reduction in mast cell burden in patients with the refractory KIT D816V mutation. Imatinib fails the gatekeeper; avapritinib walks through it.
steps.tx: **Avapritinib** is a selective KIT and PDGFRA activation-loop mutant kinase inhibitor approved for **advanced systemic mastocytosis**, demonstrating potent clinical responses and reduction in mast cell burden in patients with the refractory **KIT D816V** mutation. Imatinib fails the gatekeeper; avapritinib walks through it.
